target_customer: Consumer mobile and web app developers and growth teams that sell subscriptions
problem: App makers need to change and test paywalls, pricing and offers without shipping an app update, and need reliable subscription infrastructure behind them.
business_model: Free subscription infrastructure plus a usage fee of 1 percent of paywall-attributed revenue above 10k dollars per month (per the company's current site)
product_category: Mobile paywall experimentation and subscription infrastructure

founders.name: Jake Mor
previous_startups: Fitness AI (YC, sold at about 4 million dollars ARR)
founders.background_notes: Per a 2025 Latka interview he started building apps around age 14 and took NLP and AI classes in college; school not named.

founders.name: Brian Anglin
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no biography found in opened sources.

competitors.name: RevenueCat
competitors.what: Subscription backend and receipt validation SDK for mobile apps, a YC company
competitors.funding_then: 15 million dollar Series A in August 2020 (seed 1.5 million in 2018 per Crunchbase)

technical_complexity.rationale: A remotely configurable paywall SDK across iOS and later other platforms, with server-side purchase handling, is standard mobile engineering with some hard parts around store receipts and rendering without app releases.

defensibility.rationale: Paywalls embedded via SDK and experiment history create switching costs and a large cross-app dataset, but RevenueCat and others could add paywall editors, which they did.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: RevenueCat later shipped a paywall editor and A/B testing, so the wedge was copied. Superwall remained independent and says it was profitable as of its July 2026 post.

market_need_then: Subscription apps were growing and developers hardcoded paywalls that needed app releases to change; the founder's own Fitness AI experience with paywall testing motivated the product (per the Latka interview, which does not date this).

branding.domain_note: Operates on superwall.com, the exact .com; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and data-led, publishing paywall experiment research and benchmarks

branding.community_and_virality: Jake Mor said in a 2025 interview that the self-serve plan relies on word of mouth among mobile app founders with almost no marketing.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is known among indie and growth-focused app developers and the name literally describes the paywall, but sources show no mascot, merch or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Superwall grew from a YC Summer 2021 paywall tool into a standalone subscription platform that claims over 10,000 apps. The founder had run paywall tests at his earlier app Fitness AI, it spread by word of mouth, it reached about 3.6 million dollars ARR with 12 staff by mid 2025, and the company says it is profitable. It raised only about 7.5 million dollars in total and in July 2026 acquired the consultancy Tangent. The main risk was RevenueCat copying the paywall wedge.
notes: Total raised 7.5 million dollars per the company blog of July 2026, investors Adjacent, Acurio, Y Combinator and FJ Labs, with no round breakdown. Latka interview gives a 2 million seed and an unannounced Series A that the founder did not size; Series A is not recorded as a round because amount, date and lead are unknown. Seed date is not stated in the interview. Aggregators list 3.0 to 5 million dollar totals and a seed dated 2024, conflicting and unverified. The YC slug is staffbar, the company's earlier name; no source on the rename was found. Competitors beyond RevenueCat existing in 2021 were not sourced with dated pre-batch links.
